page: Microsoft Azure E8-2s_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the ESv3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at 2.6 GHz. This configuration provides 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled. The server is equipped with 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 32.0 GB per core. Local storage consists of a 131 GB SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPU hardware is included.

Benchmark results indicate that this instance prioritizes memory capacity over raw processing speed. In CPU-focused tests, the server registered a stress-ng single-core score of 1238.89 and a multi-core score of 1625.89, both placing in the lower performance tiers. Geekbench results align with this trend, showing a single-core score of 1062.0 and a multi-core score of 1279.0. Memory bandwidth tests recorded 90.76 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 13.94 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Database and transactional performance benchmarks showed a Passmark database operations score of 639.86 and a Redis SET throughput of 1.58 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E8-2s_v3 offers a high density of memory resources relative to its compute allocation, making it a viable option for workloads that require substantial memory capacity but have modest CPU requirements. However, the low compute and memory bandwidth benchmark scores represent a clear tradeoff for CPU-intensive applications. This server is best suited for memory-intensive workloads with low CPU utilization, such as caching layers, small relational databases, or lightweight enterprise applications requiring a large memory footprint.
